                    ### Question
                    Red-green color blindness, an X-linked recessive disorder, has an incidence of 1/200 in males in a certain population. What is the probability of a phenotypically normal male and female having a child with red-green color blindness?

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Red-green color blindness is an X-linked recessive disorder, with an incidence of 1/200 in males. A phenotypically normal male has a normal X chromosome, while a phenotypically normal female can either have two normal X chromosomes or be a carrier (one normal and one affected X chromosome). The probability of the female being a carrier is 1/200, as she must inherit the affected X from her father (who is affected) and a normal X from her mother (who is not affected). Therefore, the probability of the child inheriting the affected X from the mother is 1/200 (if she is a carrier) multiplied by 1/2 (the chance of having a son), resulting in a probability of 1/400 for a son to be affected. Thus, the correct answer is 1/400.
